change: Limiting agentic exploration to two parameter-update iterations
reason_for_change: To compare agentic parameter exploration with and without biological evidence under the same exploration budget.

decision.reason: Biologically coherent PBMC populations are present (T subsets, B, NK, mono, DC, platelets, IFN-high), but intrinsic metrics indicate weak separation (low silhouette, high DB) and several very small clusters. Clusters 0 and 1 share overlapping T-cell markers (IL7R/LTB), suggesting potential over-splitting among closely related T states. Increasing n_neighbors to 30 should smooth the graph and improve cohesion, while a modest resolution decrease to 0.8 may reduce unnecessary fragmentation among similar T/NK subsets without forcing rare but biologically plausible clusters (platelets, DC, IFN-high) to disappear. Keep n_pcs at 20 to isolate the effect of neighborhood/resolution changes.

Both evaluated settings yield similar, modest intrinsic metrics; the 30/0.8 configuration slightly improves silhouette and DB but appears to merge a plausible interferon-stimulated population seen at 15/1.0. With a smoother graph (n_neighbors=30), a modest resolution increase to 1.0 should test whether we can recover biologically coherent rare populations (e.g., ISG/DC subsets) without excessive fragmentation. Keeping n_pcs at 20 isolates the effect of resolution on structure and comparability.

final_result.final_selection_reason: 1) Strongest intrinsic metrics: Iteration 1 has the highest silhouette (0.0801) and lowest Davies–Bouldin (2.6338). Its WC-dispersion is only marginally higher than Iteration 0, and Banfield–Raftery is close to the others, making Iteration 1 the overall intrinsic-metric winner. 2) Most reasonable cluster structure: Iteration 1 yields 9 clusters with a balanced size distribution (largest ~25%) and only two very small clusters that plausibly represent rare populations (dendritic cells and platelets). Iteration 0 shows three very small clusters, suggesting mild over-fragmentation, while Iteration 2 is similar to Iteration 1 but with worse compactness (higher WC). 3) Strongest biological interpretation: Iteration 1 cleanly recovers expected PBMC populations—naive/CM T (0/1), B cells (2), classical monocytes (3), NK (4), cytotoxic T (5), non-classical/FCGR3A+ monocytes (6), dendritic cells (7), and platelets (8). Iteration 0 additionally separates a tiny interferon-stimulated cluster (ISG15/IFI6/MX1), which is biologically plausible but very small and likely reflects a shared activation program rather than a stable lineage; merging it in Iteration 1 improves robustness without losing core diversity. Iteration 2 offers no added biological resolution over Iteration 1. 4) Final selection: Iteration 1. 5) The final selection matches the intrinsic-metric winner, so no trade-off is required. Overall, Iteration 1 provides the strongest evidence by combining the best separation/compactness, a well-balanced cluster-size distribution, and clear, coherent PBMC marker patterns without unnecessary fragmentation—whereas Iteration 0 is slightly over-fragmented and Iteration 2 is intrinsically weaker without biological gain.
